name: Suryakaladi Mana (Nattassery)
tagline: A living Namboothiri mana — centre of mantravadam, Ganapathi homam and jyotisha
summary: Suryakaladi Mana at Nattassery, Kottayam is an active Namboothiri mana known for continuous mantravadam, daily Ganapathi homams and traditional jyotisha services.
description: Suryakaladi Mana is an ancestral Namboothiri mana in Nattassery (Kottayam) that continues to perform tantric rites, mantravadam and jyotisha services. The mana’s website and local reporting present it as an active centre of mantra practice and Ganapathi worship.

Tradition and the mana’s own history say the house was entrusted with tantric responsibilities (the site notes a Parasurama origin-story) and that the present palatial building was raised as an offering by Maharaja Swathi Thirunal. The mana hosts daily Ganapathi homam performed after sunrise and offers ritual services, initiations and astrological consultations.

Suryakaladi remains a living representative of Kerala’s illam tradition: it runs temple rites, organises festivals and accepts visitors and devotees (including organised pooja bookings through an online portal). For students of ritual, astrology and oral traditions it is a rare place to witness continuity of mantric practice.
highlights: Active Namboothiri mana with continuous tantric/mantric tradition
Daily Ganapathi homam performed after sunrise
House tradition links to Parasurama and historic royal patronage
Regular festival programme — large Vinayaka Chaturthi celebration (2026 programme published)
Online pooja and homam bookings available through a temple portal

sections.heading: Background
body: Suryakaladi Mana describes itself as a long-standing seat of tantra and mantravadam; its own pages and local sources emphasise a lineage of mantra practice and Ganapathi worship. Tradition recorded on the mana site says an ancestor received a sacred grantha from Surya, and successive male heads take the title 'Suryan'.

The present palatial building is recorded on the mana site as an offering from King Swathi Thirunal; the present chief named on the site is Shri Suryan Subrahmanyan Bhattathirippad. Scholarly inventories of manuscript collections and district heritage notes list Suryakaladi among Kottayam’s important manas.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Observe morning Ganapathi homam and daily rituals — the mana notes Ganapathi homam is performed after sunrise because the shrine is set within a Surya mandala. Devotees may attend darshan during poojas and festival events.

Consultations: Suryakaladi offers traditional jyotisha and mantravadam consultations, mantra deeksha and specialised homams. The mana operates an online booking portal for many services; visitors should book in advance for homams or deeksha.

Festivals and cultural programmes: the mana organises multi-day Vinayaka Chaturthi programmes with homams, music, dance and discourses (the 2026 schedule is published on the mana site). Festivals are the best time to see full-scale ritual and local participation.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Location and access: Suryakaladi Mana is in Nattassery, Perumbaikad area of Kottayam. Kottayam city and Kottayam railway station are the nearest transport hubs (the mana is a short taxi/auto ride from the station). Confirm directions locally or via the mana’s contact page before you travel.

Arrangements and etiquette: dress modestly, remove footwear before entering ritual spaces, and follow the mana’s guidance during pujas. Many services and homams require prior booking; contact the mana or use the official online booking portal to reserve a slot. Confirm visiting hours, guest-room availability or any photography rules before you go.

latest.text: Online pooja booking and a dedicated temple services portal (naamaa.in) are active for Suryakaladi Mahaganapathi Devasthanam — the portal lists homams, archana and other services available for booking.
Vinayaka Chaturthi festival at Suryakaladi Mana ran 10–15 September 2026, featuring a specially scheduled 24‑hour Ahoratra Mahaganapathi Homam and a programme of homams, performances and discourses.

visitorInfo.bestTime: Festival days (Vinayaka Chaturthi in September) for rituals; October–March for pleasant travel weather.
visitorInfo.howToReach: Reach Kottayam city by train or road, then take a taxi/auto-bus to Nattassery (the mana is a short ride from Kottayam railway station). Confirm exact directions with the mana before travel.
etiquette: Book homams, jyotisha consultations or mantra deeksha in advance via the mana’s contact page or the online portal.
Follow local temple etiquette: dress modestly, remove footwear, and ask before photographing rituals or priests.
Festival days are crowded — arrive early and confirm guest-room or prasadam arrangements before you go.
